Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 123, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Science of Mantra — Dimensions, Parallel Universes, and How "Miracles" and Black Magic Both Work

This document mer ges two consecutive teaching sessions fr om the general-audience "Mool T attva" (Sunday) series. The first piece opens with a fr esh welcome (" मूल स्वागत है... वेलकम टू आशा") and intr oduces dimensions, mantra science, and parallel universes using a physics-flavor ed "string theory" framing. The second piece has no fr esh opening of its own — it begins midconversation r esolving a question left over fr om "yester day's" class — and is mer ged her e as a dir ect continuation, extending the same dimension framework into an explanation of how black magic is claimed to work and closing with a live, individual guidance ("checking") segment for Thir d Eye Batch 4 participants. This document pr esents this teaching's own devotional/cosmological framework, illustrated with physics vocabulary (dimensions, string theory , parallel universes) used loosely and metaphorically , not as rigor ous science — see the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document. Personal details fr om the live individual-checking segment have been generalized to pr otect participants' privacy , consistent with this pr oject's standing practice; the pedagogical illustration involving two named childr en later in this document is retained as a teaching device, following this pr oject's established convention for illustrative examples, but is accompanied by strong medical-safety caveats given its life-or -death framing.
Part A — Welcome, and Ashaeiynn's Cor e Lineage

1. Session framing: Bhaiya welcomes newcomers to the Mool Tattva (foundational teaching) session, noting that some of what follows was already taught to the Third Eye batch but is being repeated here in a form intended for a broader audience seeking real understanding.

2. What Ashaeiynn is, per this teaching: Described as a mystic community devoted to Hanuman ji Maharaj, continuously channeled through the mantra "Jai Sitaram." Participants are told they are sitting among devotees of the Nath sampraday (tradition), whose guru is Hanuman ji Maharaj and whose guiding mother -ener gy is Mata Sita.

3. The mantra's traditional attribution, per this teaching: "Jai Sitaram" is described as having Mata Sita as its rishi (sage/seer), "Raam" as its beej (seed syllable), "Rim Shakti Rum" as its kilak (a traditional mantra-structure term), and as belonging to the Gayatri chandas (meter) — of fered as this teaching's own traditional attribution, not independently verified.

4. What r egular practice at Ashaeiynn is said to involve: Continuous (24-hour) chanting of "Jai Sitaram," daily negativityclearing sessions, a monthly Ram Havan, a lar ger monthly Maha Havan, and one annual Mahotsav (festival) — described as together supporting practitioners' progress toward direct experience of the guru ener gy .
Part B — The Kundalini-as-Infinity-Symbol Illustration, and Chakras as "Floors"

1. A simple visual teaching: Kundalini shakti is illustrated as a coiled, serpent-like form; tilting this coil is shown to produce an infinity-symbol ("∞") shape, used here as a loose visual metaphor for endlessness rather than a scientific claim.

2. Chakras illustrated as sequential "floors" or dimensions: The body's chakras are described, per this teaching, as a sequence of ascending "steps" or "dimensions" (first dimension, second dimension, and so on), with the practitioner's own ener gy said to climb through them as practice deepens.
Part C — Motion, Mantras, and the Concept of "Dimension" in This Teaching

1. Illustrating that nothing is ever truly still: Using Earth's simultaneous rotation and orbital motion (with an approximate figure of 29 km/second cited for orbital speed) as an example, this teaching ar gues that any "dimension" a person or mantra travels through is never a straight line but a more complex, layered, spiral-like path.
2. The four "charans" (phases) of mantra practice mapped onto early dimensions, per this teaching:

3. First dimension: a mantra that can only move forward and backward. 4. Second dimension: a mantra that can also move up and down (this corresponds to what earlier sessions called "second-charan" japa). 5. Third dimension: called a "jagrit" (awakened) mantra — corresponding to a third-charan practice, and to ordinary 3D physical space.

6. Fourth dimension: time itself; a mantra reaching this stage is said, per this teaching, to be able to "move" events forward or backward within a person's own life narrative (recorded strictly as this teaching's own devotional claim, not a claim this document treats as fact).

7. Fifth dimension and beyond, per this teaching: Introduced as the domain of parallel universes — other simultaneous "copies" of reality existing alongside one's own, which a suf ficiently developed mantra/practitioner is said to be able to access, alongside continued movement through time.

8. Sixth dimension and "omnipr esence," per this teaching: Described as the point at which a mantra (and, eventually , the practitioner) can move in every direction — forward, backward, up, down, and sideways — simultaneously; this is equated in this teaching with omnipresence, and of fered as the reason Hanuman ji Maharaj is described as present "everywhere" in a fully awakened state.

9. Higher dimensions attributed to specific deities, per this teaching: Brahma ji at the eighth or ninth dimension, Vishnu ji at the ninth or tenth, and Shiva at the tenth, with "V aikuntha" (a traditionally described celestial abode) placed at the fourteenth — of fered explicitly as this teaching's own devotional framework, paired with a passing, informal reference to real theoretical physics' use of higher -dimensional hypotheses (e.g., in some formulations of string theory) as a loose point of comparison, not a claim of equivalence.
Part D — Resolving an Appar ent Contradiction: Same "Plane," Differ ent "Dimension"
1. The question addr essed: If Hanuman ji Maharaj is said to exist at the sixth dimension, how can devotees also say he is present, in an awakened state, "right here" on Earth?

2. This teaching's r esolution: The "plane" (the underlying physical setting — here, Earth) is the same for a practitioner and for Hanuman ji Maharaj; what dif fers is the "dimension" (a kind of depth or vibrational layer) each occupies within that same plane. This teaching illustrates the idea with a loose "dream within a dream" analogy (comparable in spirit, though not detail, to the film Inception) and a passing mention of real theoretical physics proposing dozens of hypothetical dimensions (informally cited around "44"), again as a loose comparison rather than a scientific claim by this document.

3. What determines how many dimensions a practitioner's mantra can r each, per this teaching: The intensity , consistency , and repetition of practice — described loosely as a function of how much "ener gy" a practitioner has accumulated through japa, havan, guru lineage connection, or other spiritual sources.
Part E — A Parallel-Universe Healing Illustration (Sensitive: Medical Framing)

1. The illustrative example, per this teaching: Two named children present at the session, described as having the same serious illness, are used to illustrate how this teaching claims a practitioner with suf ficient "dimensional reach" might search parallel versions of a person's life/timeline for a version where the same illness resolves dif ferently , and symbolically "draw" that outcome into the person's current timeline.

2. An explicit limitation stated within this teaching itself: Bhaiya states this only works, per this teaching, if a favorable outcome genuinely exists somewhere within the practitioner's accessible range of parallel universes — if none is found, the claim is that the illness will run its course as it would have anyway . This document records this exactly as stated — as this teaching's own devotional claim about a specific, real-world medical situation — and directs readers to the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for how this must never be treated as an alternative to real medical care.

3. Why this teaching says such interventions cannot simply be sent "into space": Because the af fected pattern would eventually return to the person; the described alternative — resolving it via access to a parallel timeline — is presented as removing it more completely , per this teaching.
Part F — Black Magic and "White Magic," Per This Teaching

1. The rule stated as central to this teaching's framework: A practitioner may only draw upon their own paralleluniverse/dimensional resources. Drawing on someone else's, without their consent or a legitimate spiritual basis, is what this teaching calls "black magic" — while a devata's authorized, freely given blessing, drawing on similar mechanics, is called "white magic."

2. Why this teaching says black magic practitioners become "defaulters": Because illegitimately drawing on another being's dimension/ener gy is described as placing the practitioner at fault within a subtle-world sense of order , making them liable to correction by any more powerful spiritual authority (a "saint") who notices.

3. How saints ar e described as enfor cing this, per this teaching: Compared informally to police — able to act only once a violation is noticed ("when police aren't there, no rule; when police are there, rule applies") — with a curse or correction placed on a wrongdoer once discovered.

4. A described evasion tactic used by corrupt tantric practitioners, per this teaching: Anticipating eventual correction, such practitioners are said to maintain multiple "dummy" or decoy subtle-body identities (illustrated with a fake-driving-license analogy) tied to other , uninvolved people, so that when one identity is "caught" and cursed, an uninvolved decoy suf fers the consequence instead of the actual wrongdoer — described as a way corrupt practice is claimed to persist "for a long time."

5. A stated moral ambiguity , addr essed directly by the teacher: When asked whether this makes such outcomes unfair , Bhaiya declines to frame the discussion in explicit right/wrong terms, stating that this document (in his framing) is meant to describe how the subtle world is said to operate, not to issue an ethics class — while noting that ultimate accountability is framed within this teaching as resting with whichever party holds greater spiritual power or authority ("the greater will always face the greater ," per a proverb he cites), not framed as a general endorsement of might-makes-right by this document.

6. A personal anecdote offer ed by the teacher: Bhaiya describes an earlier period in which his own "dimension" was lowered (a setback he attributes, without detailed elaboration, to confrontations with corrupt practitioners), during which he says he
catalogued roughly 38 tantric practitioners he later confronted — of fered as a personal account, not a claim this document verifies.
Part G — Individual Guidance Segment (Third Eye Batch 4), Generalized for Privacy

1. Format of this segment: Following the theory discussion, Bhaiya conducted live, individual "checking" of Third Eye Batch 4 participants, of fering brief comments on each person's stated drishti (vision) status, described spiritual attachments, and any recommended remedial practice (such as a pitru — ancestor -related — havan). Personal, identifying details have been generalized here consistent with this project's privacy practice; the general pattern of this kind of live guidance session is recorded, not the specific individuals' case details.

2. Typical guidance patterns observed in this segment: Several participants were told they already have their "own" drishti opening and were encouraged to continue their practice without additional intervention; some were told they occasionally receive devata-mediated visions in addition to their own; several were told they have unresolved pitru (ancestral) attachment and were advised to complete one or more pitru havans as a next step; one participant described minor physical discomfort (hand pain) that was attributed, in this teaching's framing, to repetitive prayer -bead (mala) practice rather than to any negative spiritual influence.

3. A participant's account of prior mantra use for a family member's illness: One participant described using mantra-based prayer once for a relative's stomach pain, after which the discomfort resolved; Bhaiya's response af firmed the mantra's role in this teaching's framework while also noting, in the same exchange, that unfounded worry (" वह म ") itself can be harmful — this document records this exactly as discussed, and directs readers to the Bot Response Guidelines regarding never treating anecdotal accounts like this as evidence that mantra practice can replace medical care for real physical symptoms.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This document uses physics vocabulary (dimensions, string theory , parallel universes) as loose metaphor for this teaching's own devotional cosmology — it is not a claim of scientific equivalence, and must never be presented as verified physics. The parallel-universe "healing" illustration in Part E involves r eal, named childr en and a life-thr eatening illness described in the sour ce session — this document records what was said, but the Bot Response Guidelines make clear this must never be presented as an alternative to real medical treatment under any circumstance. Black magic and "white magic" ar e explained her e as differing only in consent/legitimacy of the same underlying mechanism, per this teaching — this is devotional/cosmological framing, not a claim this document endorses as literally true, and must never be used to accuse a real, identifiable person of practicing black magic. The individual guidance ("checking") segment in Part G has been generalized to pr otect r eal participants' privacy — specific personal diagnoses were not preserved verbatim. This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 123, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Science of Mantra — Dimensions, Parallel Universes, and How "Miracles" and Black Magic Both Work

Q1. What is Ashaeiynn described as, per this teaching? A1. A mystic community devoted to Hanuman ji Maharaj, continuously channeled through the mantra "Jai Sitaram," whose devotees belong to the Nath sampraday with Hanuman ji as guru and Mata Sita as guiding mother -ener gy .

Q2. What traditional attribution is given for the "Jai Sitaram" mantra? A2. Mata Sita as its rishi, "Raam" as its beej, "Rim Shakti Rum" as its kilak, and the Gayatri chandas as its meter — of fered as this teaching's own traditional attribution.

Q3. What visual teaching illustrates the concept of "infinity" in this session? A3. Kundalini shakti is illustrated as a coiled form; tilting it visually produces an infinity-symbol shape, used as a loose metaphor rather than a scientific claim.
Q4. How ar e the body's chakras described in r elation to "dimension"? A4. As a sequence of ascending "floors" or steps that a practitioner's ener gy climbs through as practice deepens.

Q5. How does this teaching map the first four "dimensions" onto stages of mantra practice? A5. First dimension: forward/backward movement only . Second dimension: also up/down (second-charan japa). Third dimension: a "jagrit" (awakened) mantra, corresponding to ordinary 3D space. Fourth dimension: time itself, with a fully developed mantra claimed (per this teaching) to be able to move events forward or backward within a person's life narrative.

Q6. What is said to exist at the fifth dimension and beyond? A6. Parallel universes — other simultaneous versions of reality a suf ficiently developed mantra/practitioner is said to be able to access.

Q7. What is described as happening at the sixth dimension? A7. Movement in every direction (forward, backward, up, down, sideways) simultaneously — equated in this teaching with omnipresence, of fered as the explanation for why Hanuman ji Maharaj is described as present everywhere in an awakened state.

Q8. Which higher dimensions ar e attributed to which deities, per this teaching? A8. Brahma ji at roughly the eighth/ninth dimension, Vishnu ji at the ninth/tenth, Shiva at the tenth, and Vaikuntha at the fourteenth — of fered as this teaching's own devotional framework, loosely compared (not equated) to real theoretical physics' higher -dimensional hypotheses.

Q9. How does this teaching r esolve the appar ent contradiction that Hanuman ji is "at the sixth dimension" yet also "her e on Earth"? A9. By distinguishing "plane" (the same physical setting, e.g., Earth) from "dimension" (a depth/vibrational layer within that plane) — the plane is shared, but the dimension occupied dif fers.

Q10. What determines how many dimensions a practitioner's mantra can r each, per this teaching? A10. The intensity , consistency , and repetition of practice, along with accumulated spiritual "ener gy" from japa, havan, and guru lineage connection.

Q1 1. What does the parallel-universe healing illustration in Part E claim, and what is the critical caveat? A1 1. It claims a suf ficiently developed practitioner might search parallel timelines for a version where a serious illness resolves favorably and symbolically draw that outcome into the present. The critical caveat, stated by the teaching itself, is that this only "works" if such a
favorable outcome exists somewhere in the practitioner's accessible range — and this document's Bot Response Guidelines make clear this must never be presented as an alternative to real medical care.

Q12. What is the differ ence between "black magic" and "white magic," per this teaching? A12. Both are said to use the same underlying mechanism (drawing on dimensional/parallel-universe resources); the dif ference is legitimacy — a practitioner may only draw on their own resources, or receive a devata's freely given blessing (white magic); drawing on someone else's without consent is called black magic.

Q13. How ar e "saints" described as enfor cing this rule? A13. Informally compared to police, who can only act once a violation is noticed — correcting or cursing a wrongdoer once discovered, not proactively monitoring everyone at all times.

Q14. What evasion tactic does this teaching describe corrupt tantric practitioners using? A14. Maintaining multiple "dummy" or decoy subtle-body identities tied to uninvolved people, so that when one identity is caught and corrected, an uninvolved decoy bears the consequence instead of the actual wrongdoer .

Q15. Did the teacher offer a moral judgment on this appar ent unfairness? A15. He declined to frame it in explicit right/wrong terms, describing the session as meant to explain how the subtle world is said to operate rather than to give an ethics lesson, while noting that within this teaching's own framework, ultimate accountability rests with whoever holds greater spiritual power or authority .

Q16. What personal anecdote did the teacher shar e about his own past? A16. That his own "dimension" was once lowered during a period of confrontation with corrupt practitioners, during which he says he catalogued roughly 38 tantric practitioners he later dealt with — of fered as a personal account, not independently verified.

Q17. What happened in the individual guidance ("checking") segment at the end of this session? A17. Bhaiya gave brief, live comments to several Third Eye Batch 4 participants about their drishti status and any recommended next steps (such as a pitru havan); personal details have been generalized in this document to protect participants' privacy .

Q18. What common patterns appear ed acr oss the individual guidance given? A18. Several participants were told they already have their own drishti opening and could continue practicing; some were told they occasionally also receive devata-mediated visions; several were advised to complete pitru havans for unresolved ancestral attachment; one described minor hand discomfort attributed to repetitive prayer -bead practice rather than negative influence.

Q19. What did one participant shar e about prior mantra use, and what should a bot never conclude fr om it? A19. She described mantra-based prayer once coinciding with resolution of a relative's stomach pain. A bot must never treat this anecdote as evidence that mantra practice can replace medical care for a real person's physical symptoms.
Bot Response Guidelines

1. Present all dimension/parallel-universe/black-magic content in this document as this teaching's own devotional cosmology , illustrated loosely with physics vocabulary — never as verified physics, and never as a technique guide a user could apply .

2. Never present the parallel-universe "healing" framework, or any claim in this document, as an alternative to r eal medical diagnosis or treatment, under any cir cumstance — including for cancer or any other serious illness. If a user raises a real medical situation, encourage them to seek qualified medical care; do not suggest spiritual practice as a substitute.

3. Never use the "black magic" framework in this document to accuse, diagnose, or speculate about a r eal, identifiable person practicing black magic against the user or anyone else. Treat such requests as outside what this bot can responsibly do, and redirect toward general reassurance and, if genuine distress is present, professional support.
4. Never validate a user's account of "curses," "dummy subtle bodies," or spiritual r etribution as objectively r eal — these are recorded here as this teaching's own devotional narrative device.

5. The individual guidance segment (Part G) has alr eady been generalized for privacy in this document — never attempt to r econstruct or guess the r eal identities or specific personal details behind it, and never perform a similarly personal "spiritual diagnosis" of a r eal bot user .

6. If a user shar es an account similar to the mantra-and-r elative's-illness anecdote, r espond with warmth but do not affirm a causal spiritual mechanism for a r eal medical outcome; encourage appr opriate medical follow-up for any ongoing symptoms.
7. This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document.
8. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
